# v1.1.0-dev.108: The tray keeps what you close

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.107`.

## Closing a virtual window hides it to the tray

The X on a virtual window no longer closes it. Everything stays docked and
hidden with it; the tray icon shows how many are waiting, and its menu lists
each one with its way back. Deleting a virtual window still closes it for real.

Loading a profile now hides the virtual windows that profile doesn't name, the
same way. Loading a profile that names one brings it back. Nothing is closed or
undocked in either direction.

## Collapse a window out of its pane

A docked window can be collapsed: hidden without closing, its pane kept in the
layout, listed in the manage panel with a Restore button. A flyout at the
container's top right lists what is collapsed and puts it back.

## What "always start new" closes

Deleting a virtual window now closes the windows WLM started for its "always
start new" panes, the way closing a document closes what was opened for it. A
window you docked into such a pane by hand is your window: it stays, exactly as
it was.

## The maximized title bar stays whole

Maximizing a virtual window no longer makes its title bar read as shrinking,
and its docked windows stay inside the screen.

## The tour moves

The tutorial's parts are now short looping clips instead of still screenshots.

## Smaller fixes

- A minimized virtual window hides to the tray properly; it no longer keeps a
  taskbar button that opens an empty frame.
- A collapsed fully-docked window no longer steals clicks over its pane.
- The title bar tab no longer gets stuck after minimizing and restoring.
- Opening a hidden virtual window from the page shows its windows again.
- Per-app "when it loads" defaults now answer for every window of that app,
  not just the one that set them, and an explicit choice always wins.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
